Moody’s Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi cautioned that forecasts for consumer spending lack solid fundamentals, stating his growing unease over wage stagnation, dwindling savings, and rising borrowing costs.

Pushback on Consumer Resilience

During the latest Inside Economics podcast, Zandi challenged the prevailing narrative of consumer durability championed by Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) Chief Economist Wayne Best.

While Best forecasted a 2.2% real GDP growth for 2026 and cited ongoing consumer “resilience,” Zandi argued the macroeconomic data does not support a robust outlook for lower- and middle-income households.

"I am getting more nervous the less nervous you guys sound," Zandi told his co-hosts and Best. "It just feels like we’re too optimistic about the consumer."

Zandi pointed to flat real wage growth, a drop in the savings rate, and rising interest rates as core concerns. He noted that after-tax income adjusted for inflation is “not going anywhere,” and consumers lack the ability to extract cash through home refinancing due to mortgage rates sitting well over 7%.

"Something doesn’t compute," Zandi stated, questioning how the economy sustains steady growth under such financial strain.

Read Also: Fed’s Goolsbee Warns AI Data Center Boom Could Overheat US Economy — ‘The Bigger The Hype,’ The Bigger The Risk

Inflation and Interest Rate Pressures

Best maintained that consumers are finding ways to navigate higher prices through price shopping and the temporary boost from tax refunds. He stated that an income proxy measuring wages, hours worked, and employment remains steady, showing growth of around 4%.

However, Zandi and Moody’s Analytics Senior Director of Global Forecasting Marisa DiNatale highlighted the prolonged impact of geopolitical conflicts on diesel and jet fuel prices, which they argued are eating into disposable income. DiNatale expressed specific concern for the bottom 40% of income earners, noting they are spending a larger share of their budgets on essentials.

Zandi added that rising yields are exacerbating the situation, pointing out that credit card and auto loan rates are climbing as the Federal Reserve continues to tighten monetary policy.

"If the equity market hangs tough, then that should be okay," Zandi said regarding affluent spenders. But for the broader public facing higher prices without real wage gains, he maintained his skepticism about near-term consumer strength.

How Have Stocks Performed in 2026?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 11.84% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 15.33%, and the Dow Jones gained 6.13% YTD.

On Tuesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed mixed. SPY fell 0.18% to $764.20, while QQQ rose 0.19% to $737.93. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 0.22% lower at $512.88.

In premarket trading on Tuesday, SPY was up 0.18%, QQQ dipped 0.08%, and DIA was down 0.01%.

Carmax Inc (NYSE:KMX) on Tuesday reported better-than-expected second-quarter financial results.

CarMax reported adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share, beating the analyst estimate of 73 cents. Sales rose 19.5% year over year to $7.88 billion, beating the $6.98 billion estimate.

Retail used-vehicle sales rose 13.8% to 227,391 units, while comparable-store used-vehicle sales increased 13%. Retail revenue climbed 19.7%, helped by higher sales volume and a $1,600, or 6.3%, increase in the average selling price.

“Our strong second quarter results reflect solid execution and early progress against Shift into GEAR, our four-pillar strategy to strengthen CarMax’s core business and return the company to sustained growth,” said Keith Barr, President and Chief Executive Officer. “We delivered 81% EPS growth as we strengthened our price competitiveness, increased Extended Protection Plan margins, expanded CAF’s share of Tier 2 originations, continued to enhance our digital experience, and drove material SG&A leverage. I am confident in our ability to build on this early momentum. We have a clear strategy, a solid foundation, and an exceptional team accelerating our progress to create long-term value for our shareholders.”

CarMax shares fell 0.3% to $59.06 in pre-market trading.

These analysts made changes to their price targets on CarMax following earnings announcement.

  • B of A Securities analyst John Murphy maintained the stock with an Underperform rating and raised the price target from $45 to $50.
  • BNP Paribas analyst Chris Bottiglieri reiterated the stock with an Underperform rating and raised the price target from $33 to $48.

UiPath, Inc. (NYSE:PATH) shares are up by about half a percent during Wednesday’s premarket session.

On Tuesday, the company expanded its partnership with BDO USA to develop AI and business orchestration solutions for key enterprise functions.

It includes risk management, controls transformation, enterprise compliance and other Office of the CFO activities.

Expands BDO Partnership For Agentic Automation

The companies will jointly develop AI agents designed to automate and oversee these functions.

The collaboration includes Agentic Internal Audit Solution Accelerators aimed at modernizing IT Application Controls (ITAC) and IT General Controls (ITGC).

The tools are designed to replace labor-intensive testing with agent-driven processes supported by professional reviews, while helping monitor controls, gather evidence, perform testing and identify exceptions more efficiently.

The update reinforces UiPath’s push to package automation into repeatable, deployable solutions that can shorten time-to-value for enterprise customers.

PATH Technical Outlook: Key Levels And Momentum

PATH Trend Versus Key Moving Averages

At $12.38, PATH is trading 12.8% below its 20-day SMA ($14.19) and 14.4% below its 50-day SMA ($14.46), which keeps the intermediate trend biased lower despite the premarket uptick. The stock is also about 3% below its 100-day SMA ($12.76) and about 2.8% below its 200-day SMA ($12.74), putting it in a tight zone where longer-term trend support is close but not yet reclaimed.

MACD Signals Cooling Momentum

MACD is the cleaner momentum lens right now: it’s below its signal line and the histogram is negative, which points to upside pressure cooling versus the prior upswing. In plain terms, when MACD sits below its signal line, it often means rallies can fade unless buyers step in with enough force to flip momentum back in their favor.

Support And Resistance Levels To Watch

The bigger-picture backdrop is mixed: the golden cross in August (50-day moving above the 200-day) is still a longer-term constructive marker, but price action has weakened since the recent swing high in September. With the stock down 7.92% over the last 12 months and sitting well below the short-term averages, bulls generally need to prove they can reclaim overhead levels before the trend looks healthier.

  • Key Resistance: $13.00 — a round-number area that also sits near the 200-day EMA ($13.02), making it a logical spot where rebounds can stall
  • Key Support: $12.50 — a nearby round-number level just above current price that can act as a first "line in the sand" if selling pressure returns

Accenture plc (NYSE:ACN) will release its fourth-quarter earnings report before the opening bell on Thursday, Oct. 1.

Some of Accenture’s investors may be eyeing potential gains from the company’s dividends. As of now, ACN has an annual dividend yield of 3.68%, with a quarterly dividend of $1.63 per share ($6.52 a year).

To figure out how to earn $500 monthly from Accenture, we start with the yearly target of $6,000 ($500 x 12 months).

Next, we divide that amount by ACN’s $6.52 dividend: $6,000 / $6.52 = 920 shares.

So, an investor would need to own approximately $162,950 worth of Accenture, or 920 shares to generate a monthly dividend income of $500.

Assuming a more conservative goal of $100 monthly ($1,200 annually), we do the same calculation: $1,200 / $6.52 = 184 shares, or $32,590 to generate a monthly dividend income of $100.

Note that dividend yield can change on a rolling basis, as dividend payments and stock prices both fluctuate over time.

The dividend yield is calculated by dividing the annual dividend payment by the current stock price. As the stock price changes, the dividend yield will also change.

For example, if a stock pays an annual dividend of $2 and its current price is $50, its dividend yield would be 4%. However, if the stock price increases to $60, the dividend yield would decrease to 3.33% ($2/$60).

Conversely, if the stock price decreases to $40, the dividend yield would increase to 5% ($2/$40).

Further, the dividend payment itself can also change over time, which can impact the dividend yield. If a company increases its dividend payment, the dividend yield will increase even if the stock price remains the same. Similarly, if a company decreases its dividend payment, the dividend yield will decrease.

On CNBC’s “Mad Money Lightning Round,” Jim Cramer said Fermi Inc. (NASDAQ:FRMI) “should never have come public. It’s the kind of thing that got caught up in the mania. It came public, lost people a lot of money.”

The Texas-based real estate investment trust went public on Oct. 1, 2025, about a year ago. It priced its IPO at $21 a share the night before, Sept. 30, 2025, and began trading on the Nasdaq and the London Stock Exchange the next day.

On its first day, Fermi opened about 19% above the IPO price.

On the earnings front, Fermi reported a second-quarter loss of 4 cents per share on Aug. 13, versus the analyst consensus estimate of a loss of 7 cents per share.

Cramer said he doesn’t want to put anybody anywhere near anything aerospace right now, when asked about HEICO Corporation (NYSE:HEI).

Guggenheim analyst Michael Ciarmoli initiated coverage on Heico on Sept. 15 with a Neutral rating.

When asked about Grab Holdings Limited (NYSE:GRAB), he said, “I don’t know what’s going to turn that thing around.”

In recent news, the company announced on Sept. 15 a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling 60% equity interest in Atome Financial for $1.49 billion in cash.

Price Action

  • Fermi shares gained 0.5% to settle at $4.28 on Tuesday.
  • Heico shares rose 0.8% to close at $307.11 during the session.
  • Grab rose 0.8% to settle at $3.12 on Tuesday.

The U.S. military is preparing to end its presence in Iraq, which began during the fight against ISIS, with a total withdrawal of troops scheduled for Wednesday.

The withdrawal was negotiated under the Biden administration in 2024 and continued under President Donald Trump, with Sept. 30 set as the final pullout date. During the U.S. military presence in Iraq, about 4,500 U.S. service members died, mostly between 2003 and 2011, ABC News reported.

The U.S. withdrew from Iraq in 2011 after an eight-year military presence that began with the 2003 invasion. American troops returned in 2014 after ISIS seized territory in Iraq and Syria, and remained after ISIS’s military defeat in 2019 to help prevent a resurgence.

The Pentagon spokesperson, Sean Parnell, stated that the U.S. and coalition partners have formally ended Operation Inherent Resolve, while continuing targeted training and intelligence support for Iraqi forces.

At the same time, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi said the end of the international coalition’s mission marks Iraq’s shift toward taking full responsibility for its own security and stability, rather than an end to the fight against terrorism.

Will Iran Increase Influence in Iraq?

The U.S. has been steadily reducing its military presence in Iraq, consolidating forces in the north and quietly withdrawing troops from Erbil since the war with Iran began in February. After several months of drawdowns, only a limited U.S. presence remains in northern Iraq.

The U.S.-Iran war has altered the regional dynamics between Iraq and the U.S. Iraq’s Shiite ties with Iran and Tehran’s military support for Shiite militias inside Iraq raise questions about Iran’s future influence in Iraq.

Iraq Looks Beyond Hormuz

The U.S. withdrawal from Iraq also comes at a time when the country is seeking to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic chokepoint for global oil supplies.

In July, Iraq and Syria agreed to revive a long-idled oil pipeline linking northern Iraq to Syria’s Mediterranean coast. The move, overseen by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright, was aimed at bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The agreement was signed during a U.S.-Iraq investment summit in Washington by Basra Oil Company CEO Bassem Abdul Karim Nasr and Syrian Petroleum Company CEO Youssef Qablawi.

Wright said at the time that Iraq has significant potential to increase oil production, reduce reliance on hostile neighbors, and expand energy access, prosperity, and economic freedom.

Notably, Iraq’s oil revenues have historically been held through accounts linked to the Central Bank of Iraq at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. As per the arrangement, created under former President George W. Bush, the U.S.-led Coalition Provisional Authority established the Development Fund for Iraq after the 2003 invasion to collect oil income for reconstruction and protect it from legal claims tied to Saddam Hussein’s regime.

Ripple has partnered with CSD BR, one of Brazil’s central securities depositories, to bring the XRP Ledger into the country’s regulated financial infrastructure for the first time.

How the Partnership Actually Works

Ripple announced Tuesday that CSD BR will start using the XRP Ledger to record and audit financial assets, beginning with BTG Pactual investment fund shares. 

CSD BR keeps full control over registration, deposit, and settlement, and the blockchain simply adds a second layer where everyone can check that the records match up in near real time.

The scale here is significant: CSD BR oversees more than BRL 22 trillion, roughly $4.3 trillion, in registered assets. 

The fund shares run through Ripple’s tokenization standard and mirror onto the XRP Ledger, though access stays limited to banks and corporate clients in Brazil who still go through standard KYC and anti-money laundering checks. 

Regulators and courts also retain leverage over the system, since CSD BR can freeze assets or reverse transactions whenever ordered to.

“We chose to start with record mirroring because it is the safest and most responsible way to introduce a new technology into critical market infrastructure,” said Daniel Polano Spreafico, Head of Products and Clients at CSD BR.

Why This Matters Beyond a Pilot

Ripple Managing Director for Latin America Silvio Pegado called the partnership a major milestone, noting it moves distributed ledger technology past pilots and proofs of concept into live record-keeping infrastructure inside a national capital market. 

Once the mirroring phase gets validated, the plan expands to native asset issuance and trading, with Real Estate and Agribusiness Receivables Certificates under consideration as major segments of Brazil’s fixed income market.

BTG Pactual Partner Luis Furtado said the deal lets the bank apply blockchain directly to the fund market while keeping current processes and the official asset record intact.

XRP Technical Analysis

XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) is up 1.5% Wednesday, consolidating inside a large symmetrical triangle that has compressed price since July. 

Lower highs from the August peak near $1.70 keep meeting higher lows off the $1 base, a classic coiling pattern that typically resolves with a volatility expansion. 

Price holds above every major EMA, with RSI at 57.90 sitting neutral after cooling from August’s overbought spike.

Key levels for XRP:

  • $1.70 — August high, next major target
  • $1.46 — 20-day EMA, immediate support
